Here is a chart to illustrate my question:

I feel like I'm getting really close to having a breakthrough moment, but I'm missing some pieces. Not all DP's react...even ones that occur at S/R swap levels. Often times they fail. Does this have to do with the MPL? I understand the FTR PAZ, but the other types of PAZ still confuse me and the MPL is also something I don't completely understand.

It has been written many times in the RTM forums that IT's want the best possible price..Conceptually this makes sense...if I want to sell I am looking for the highest possible price to do so in order to maximize my return. Assuming I am an IT looking to short, I want to sell at the highest price possible (This is the MPL). If I am looking at a chart, there are dozens of places where I could turn price...and there will always be a supply zone or DP or FTR that exists at a price higher than current price. So when RTM traders say IT's want the best possible price, they are talking about a price level that is best within the context of the current trade setup...not necessarily the best price (hypothetically speaking, you could wait forever for price to keep climbing before shorting. There is always another level higher up).

Does this question make any sense?I am not very good at describing these concepts using words. Maybe this picture will help:

This level looks pretty good - it followed a fakeout and subsequent engulf. It acted at the origin of a major down move. Price blew through it and instead turned at a supply level higher up.
